rationale: Owner ruled RFC_042 §6 = option (c) on 2026-08-22: commission the unified content-loss detector, executed as bugs_open/355 prescribes — A1 (writer attribution) first, then A2+A3 (detector + reader, one commit), A4 (refusal) deferred until a population exists. This submission covers the two halves already committed that make the detector's INSTRUMENT complete and attributable; the detector binary itself is cmd/ (out of gate scope) and follows. Half 1, migration 552 (commit e7567d1fc): 357's archive trigger is AFTER UPDATE OF rendered_html gated on the html changing, so a content_data-only UPDATE — the one change the content-loss class is about — archives nothing. Measured at HEAD: every Go in-place writer sets both columns in one UPDATE except the admin handler's dynamic SET list, which is the live producer of the blind shape, plus raw psql and every future writer. A second trigger on the SAME function fires exactly when 357's cannot (WHEN clauses mutually exclusive on NEW.rendered_html IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.rendered_html — no UPDATE can double-archive), skips '{}' pre-images, keeps 357's fail-closed posture (RFC_017), and its probe exercises all five arms selecting rows BY BYTES (357's own probe failed its first apply on same-xact created_at ordering). Deliberate redundancy stated in the header: this arm archives the unchanged html bytes rather than adding a second code path through a fail-closed function. Half 2, A1 (commits 8552e621d + 0702fb9cb): page_component_history.application_name has only ever held pgbouncer's socket stamp (app - <ip>:<port>, one value per CONNECTION, several writers per binary) — the archive pairs before/after perfectly and can attribute nothing, which is the exact question RFC_042 §4.3 names as the detector's purpose (which writers actually lose keys in practice). The form is SELECT set_config('application_name', $1, true) INSIDE the same transaction as the write; both halves load-bearing: SET/SET LOCAL take no bind parameters (355 §A1's original sketch was unrunnable — caught by the parallel 238 session), and under pgbouncer pool_mode=transaction a session-level SET would leak the stamp onto other clients' work while is_local=true dies at COMMIT. Only 2 of 9 write sites hold a transaction today (parallel session's census, verified), so stampedExecContext wraps the four bare-autocommit UPDATE writers in a short tx — on autocommit, set_config(...,true) is a statement-scoped no-op. Best-effort by construction: Begin failure and stamp failure both fall back to the unstamped statement; attribution must never break the write. Mutation-proven: M1 (delete the stamp) fails TestStampedExecStampsInsideTheSameTransaction; M2 (is_local=false) fails the same test on the pinned SQL text; M3 (stamp failure aborting the write) fails TestStampedExecStampFailureStillWrites. Deliberately NOT stamped, stated in the helper header so nobody 'finishes' it: save_page_sections (the funnel — its rows are already discriminated by op='delete', and its archive/DELETE/INSERTs are separate autocommit statements whose wrapping would change crash behaviour) and the INSERT-only writers (INSERT is never archived; no row to attribute). No new config keys; optional-key budget untouched (plan_sections stays 7/10). Acceptance at the artefact after the next roll: SELECT DISTINCT application_name FROM page_component_history WHERE created_at > now() - interval '1 day' shows action:*/admin-edit values — nothing else in the codebase sets application_name (grep-verified 2026-08-22), so any such value is provably this mechanism.

func stampedExecContext(ctx, db, writer, query string, args ...interface{}) (sql.Result, error) { tx, err := db.BeginTx(ctx, nil); if err != nil { return db.ExecContext(ctx, query, args...) } ... }

plan.risks: The 552 trigger is fail-closed like 357: a broken history table halts content_data-only page writes loudly — the RFC_017 posture, chosen over a silent recreation of the loss class; its blast radius today is admin edits (the only live content-only writer). The short-tx wrap changes four writers from one autocommit statement to a three-statement transaction — atomicity of the single write is unchanged, and both failure modes fall back to the exact pre-A1 statement; the residual risk is pgbouncer treating the extra tx traffic differently, bounded by these writers' low volume (section edits, dossier renders, blog rebuilds). Stamp values are compile-time constants, never user input. The archive grows by the content-only arm's volume (admin edits today; the detector's daily heartbeat reports pair volumes so growth is watched). 552 is committed but NOT applied — apply follows this verdict.
plan.non_scope: The detector binary itself (cmd/content-loss-check — cmd/ is outside the gate's footprint; its design is recorded in bugs_open/355 and the lane docs). save_page_sections' transactional shape (named as a real observation — its archive/DELETE/INSERTs are separate statements and a crash mid-loop leaves a half-replaced page — but changing it is not attribution work; recorded in 355). The INSERT-only writers (no archive row exists to attribute; the detector's current-state census covers born-incomplete rows). A4 refusal arming (owner-deferred until A2/A3 produce a population). RFC_008's rendered_html seam (explicitly not ruled by the owner's option-c decision).
